info.title: UNA API
info.summary: REST API v2 of a UNA community site.
info.description:
Preview: API v2 is not ready for production. Shapes and paths may still change, and a site turns it on in Studio > API > Settings (off as installed).

Resource URLs, HTTP methods, JSON bodies and real status codes.

Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code`, `type` `urn:una:problem:<code>`; `errors` lists invalid fields.

Lists are `{items, next_cursor}` with cursor paging: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; it is always there, `null` on the last page. Ids are decimal strings.

JSON answers of 200 to GET up to 1 MiB carry a weak ETag (`W/"<hex>"`, a digest of the body) with `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`; send it back as `If-None-Match` (compared weakly; a list and `*` work too) to get 304 with no body while nothing changed. Errors and writes carry none.

Requests are rate limited by kind (reads, writes, searches, link previews, messages to agents, uploads), a signed-in one by its profile and a guest's by its address: one over the limit is 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`, the seconds until it may be sent again.

Signed-in writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) honour `Idempotency-Key` (1 to 255 visible ASCII characters): a repeat with the same key and request gets the first answer again, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, for a day; the same key with another request is 422 `idempotency_key_reused`, and one while the first still runs 409 `idempotency_in_progress`. Uploads (multipart) and guests' requests ignore it.

The previous API (`api.php`, v1) is unchanged.

get.summary: What this API is and how to sign in
get.description: A client that only knows the site URL starts here: it finds the OpenAPI document, the OAuth endpoints and which modules this site's API has (`modules`), so it shows a section only where the site has one.

get.summary: One activity of a feed

delete.summary: Remove an activity from the feeds
delete.description: For a feed post this deletes the post. For content of another module it removes the activity only; the content stays in its module.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: The AI agents the viewer may chat with
get.description: The site's agents (Studio > Agents) the viewer may talk to: active, meant for people (trigger `manual` or `message`) and with the viewer's membership level among theirs ("Visible for"; administrators may talk to every one). `default_id` is the site's operator agent (Studio > Settings > Agents, `sys_agents_operator_agent`) when the viewer may talk to it, else the first one, else null: a client shows no agent chat at all without one. Guests get the agents guests may talk to (an empty list on most sites).

get.summary: The viewer's chats with an agent, the latest first
get.description: The viewer's own chats with the agent (the history the site's chat widget lists), the most recently active first, at most 50. A closed chat with nothing in it is left out. 403 for an agent the viewer may not talk to.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

post.summary: Start a new chat with an agent
post.description: A new, empty chat of the viewer's with the agent, listed at once (as the site widget's New chat). The chats before stay open. 403 for an agent the viewer may not talk to.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: One of the viewer's chats with an agent, with its messages
get.description: The chat and its messages, oldest first: what the person wrote and what the agent answered, as text (Markdown, as written) and as HTML (the text through Markdown in safe mode, as the site turns an agent's reply into a Messenger message), without the tools' results. A chat of someone else's, or of another agent, is 404, as is one in a context.

parameters.name: chat
parameters.description: The chat's id: `default` or its nonce

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

post.summary: Write to an agent and read its reply as it is written
post.description: A turn of the chat: the viewer's message, and the agent's reply streamed as Server-Sent Events while the agent writes it (`text/event-stream`, each event `data: <JSON>`, an AgentEvent). These are AG-UI's events, the ones the site's chat widget reads: `RUN_STARTED`; `TEXT_MESSAGE_START`, `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` with the next piece of the reply in `delta` (Markdown), `TEXT_MESSAGE_END`; tool calls (`TOOL_CALL_*`); `CUSTOM` events named `chat_actions` (buttons the agent offers, `value.actions`) and `chat_session` (`value.closed`: the agent closed the chat); then `RUN_FINISHED`, or `RUN_ERROR` with `message` when the agent could not answer (no model set up, the model failed, the session limit). The chat keeps both messages, so GET /agents/{id}/chats/{chat} has them, the reply as HTML too. Closing the connection stops the reply. The message is text, at most the agent's `max_input_chars` (8000 when it sets none). A chat that does not exist yet is started by it (as the site widget does). 403 for an agent the viewer may not talk to, 404 for a chat of someone else's.

parameters.name: chat
parameters.description: The chat's id: `default` or its nonce

schema.description: Events `data: <JSON>` separated by a blank line, each JSON one AgentEvent

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: Albums the viewer may see, newest first or in another order
get.description: As the site's browse pages list them: active albums, with the module's privacy, so a page can have fewer items than `limit` and still a `next_cursor`. `sort`: `recent` (the default, newest first), `updated`, `popular` (most viewed), `top` (most liked) or `featured` (featured ones only). `author` keeps one profile's albums, `context` (or `context_id`) those in a group or other context: 422 for one that is no context or that the viewer may not know of, 403 for one whose content the viewer may not see.

parameters.name: author
parameters.description: A profile id

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Only albums in this group (or other context): its profile id

parameters.name: context_id
parameters.description: The same as `context` (v2 only)

post.summary: Make an album, with photos in it or empty
post.description: Through the site's album form. `title` is needed (the form's length limits apply: 422 with its message). `media_ids` are up to 50 of the viewer's uploads of purpose `album` (POST /uploads) that nothing took yet (422 otherwise, 415 for one that is no photo), its items in this order, each titled with its file name. `text_html` is user HTML the site filters (or plain text, each line a paragraph). `context_id` puts it in a group (or another context) whose members may add albums there (403 otherwise); its audience is then the context's, so `audience` may not be sent with it. `comments_enabled` false is 422: the site can't turn comments off. The uploads are photos only (the site's own pages add videos too).

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: An album, with what the viewer may do with it
get.description: Counts a view, as opening it on the site does (once a day per viewer). 404 when there is none (or it is hidden or waiting for approval, and the viewer is not its author or a moderator; or it is in a secret group or other context the viewer may not know of), 403 when the viewer may not see it. Its items are GET /albums/{id}/items, its comments GET /content/{content_id}/comments.

patch.summary: Change an album's title, text or audience
patch.description: One's own, or any for moderators (the module's edit check; 403 otherwise). A new audience is its items' too, as they are seen by whom the album is. `audience` is not for one in a context (422).

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Delete an album and what is in it
delete.description: One's own where the membership level may delete albums, or any for administrators (the module's delete check; 403 otherwise). Its items, their files and comments, and its activity in the feeds go with it, as on the site.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: The photos and videos in an album, in its order
get.description: In the order the album's page shows them. 404 and 403 as GET /albums/{id}. An item is the album's own (its `id` is the item's, `album_id` the album's), not an entry of Photos or Videos, so GET /photos/{id} does not answer for it; it has no Item (`content_id` null), so its comments and likes stay on the site, and its viewer's `can_edit` and `can_delete` are what the album's author may do there.

post.summary: Add photos to an album, at its end
post.description: As the site's Add images form adds them: `media_ids` are up to 50 of the viewer's uploads of purpose `album` that nothing took yet (422 otherwise, 415 for one that is no photo), added at the end in this order, each titled with its file name. Only the album's author adds here, where the membership level lets them edit it (403 otherwise: the site's form takes its author's uploads only). The answer is the new items, in this order; when the site does not take them all it is 422 and the uploads are the viewer's again, taken by nothing. Uploads of purpose `album` are open to who may make albums or has one.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

patch.summary: Edit a comment: one's own, or any for moderators
patch.description: `body` (plain text) or `body_html` (as in NewComment) replaces the whole comment. A plain-text `body` would lose a comment's links, mentions or formatting, so for such a comment it answers 409 formatted_text: send `body_html`. 409 comments_disabled when the item takes no comments.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Delete a comment: its author, the author of the item it is on, or a moderator
delete.description: A comment with replies can be deleted only by a moderator, and its replies go with it; others get 409.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: Replies to a comment, oldest first
get.description: The replies shown under the comment. A site nests replies a set number of levels deep (the Timeline: one): the replies to a comment at the deepest level are shown, and listed, under its parent, so this lists the whole thread under a top-level comment. `parent_id` of each one says which comment it answers. 409 comments_disabled when the item takes no comments.

get.summary: What an activity shows: a feed post, or content of another module
get.description: The id is an Item id, as in Activity.object.id and Comment.target_id. 404 when it does not exist (or was deleted), 403 when the viewer may not see it.

get.summary: Top-level comments of an item, pinned first, then oldest first
get.description: Replies are listed by GET /comments/{id}/replies. 409 comments_disabled when the item takes no comments.

post.summary: Comment on an item, or reply to a comment of it
post.description: Send `body` (plain text: the site keeps it as written, a literal `<` included) or `body_html` (HTML as the site's comment editor writes it: paragraphs, line breaks, links, mentions and hashtags; the site filters it as its comment form does, and indexes its mentions and hashtags), not both. A comments object that keeps text only stores `body_html` as its text. 409 comments_disabled when the item takes no comments.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

put.summary: Set the viewer's reaction to an item
put.description: Idempotent: setting the reaction the viewer already gave changes nothing. Where one reaction per person is allowed, a new one replaces the old one. 409 reactions_disabled when the item takes no reactions.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Take back the viewer's reactions to an item
delete.description: 409 reactions_disabled when the item takes no reactions.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: The viewer's inbox, latest reply first

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

post.summary: Start a conversation
post.description: Recipients the viewer may not contact are left out, as on the site (422 when that leaves nobody). `media_ids` are the viewer's uploads of purpose `conversation` (POST /uploads), shown with the first message in the order given; anything else is 422 on `media_ids[i]`. Find recipients with GET /search/profiles.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: How many messages in the inbox the viewer has not read

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: A conversation of the viewer

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: Replies in a conversation, newest first
get.description: The first page holds the newest replies; each next page the ones before it (a keyset cursor, so replies that come meanwhile shift nothing). `before` (a message id) starts a page before that message, for a client that knows one. The message that started the conversation is its `body`; this lists what came after it. A message's id grows with time.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only replies older than this message; `cursor`, when given, wins

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

post.summary: Reply in a conversation
post.description: `media_ids` are the viewer's uploads of purpose `message` (POST /uploads), shown with the message in the order given; anything else is 422 on `media_ids[i]`. The site needs text with every message.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

patch.summary: Edit one's own reply in a conversation
patch.description: `body` replaces the whole text: HTML as the site's message editor writes it (paragraphs, line breaks, links, mentions), which the site filters as its form does. Only the reply's author, and only where the site lets them edit it (the conversation's own edit check, which lets administrators alone edit messages on a site as installed; `can_edit` says): 403 otherwise. Its photos stay. The message that started the conversation is the conversation's text, not a reply: it is not edited here. A message of another conversation, or none, is 404.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

post.summary: Add people to a conversation
post.description: Only who started it may, where the site lets them edit it (`can_add_participants`), as the site's edit form has the recipients for the author only (403 otherwise). People the viewer may not contact are left out, as when starting one; 422 when that leaves nobody new. Those added see the whole conversation, unread.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Leave a conversation, or take someone out of one
delete.description: The viewer's own id leaves it (`can_leave`, the site's delete check), as deleting it from the trash does on the site: it is gone from the viewer's inbox for good, and once nobody is left the conversation is deleted. Another participant can be taken out only by who started it, where the site lets them edit it (403 otherwise). As on the site, a reply brings who started it back in. One who is not in it is 404.

parameters.name: profile_id
parameters.description: A profile in the conversation

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

post.summary: Mark every message of a conversation as read

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Mark a conversation as unread, as the site's Mark unread does
delete.description: Every message of it counts as unread for the viewer again, the first one too. One that is unread already (a conversation just received) stays so: 204 again.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: Discussions the viewer may see, the most recently replied to first
get.description: As the site's browse pages list them: active discussions, with the module's privacy, so a page can have fewer items than `limit` and still a `next_cursor`. `sort` `latest` (the default) orders by the last reply (a discussion without replies by when it started), `new` by when it started, `featured` keeps the featured ones, the last featured first (the site's Featured Discussions). `category` keeps one category (GET /discussions/categories), `context_id` the discussions in a group (or another context) the viewer may see; a context the viewer may not see is 403.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: A category id

parameters.name: context_id
parameters.description: A group's (or other context's) profile id

post.summary: Start a discussion
post.description: Send `body` (plain text: each line is a paragraph, and a literal `<` stays text) or `body_html` (HTML as the site's editor writes it: formatting, lists, quotes, code, links, mentions, hashtags and pictures; the site's form filters it and indexes its mentions and hashtags), not both. Without `category_id` the first category is used. `context_id` puts it in a group (or another context) whose members may post discussions there (403 otherwise); its audience is then the group's, so `audience` may not be sent with it (422). The site's own checks of the form apply (422 with its message for a field it refuses).

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: The categories a discussion can be in, and whether the viewer may start one
get.description: The categories the site's form for a new discussion offers, in its order. `can_create` says whether POST /discussions would be accepted (the membership level may create discussions); false for guests. With `counts=true` each has `count`, as the site's Categories block counts its discussions (GET /discussions?category= lists them).

parameters.name: counts
parameters.description: Add `count` to each category: how many items it has, as the site's Categories block counts them (active, and public or for members)

get.summary: A discussion, with what the viewer may do with it
get.description: Counts a view, as opening it on the site does (once a day per viewer). 404 when there is none (or it was deleted, or it is hidden or waiting for approval and the viewer is not its author or a moderator; or it is in a secret group or other context the viewer may not know of), 403 when the viewer may not see it (one in a closed group from outside). Its replies are GET /content/{content_id}/comments.

patch.summary: Edit a discussion: its title, text or category
patch.description: One's own, or any for moderators and the admins of the group it is in (the module's edit check; 403 otherwise). `body` (plain text) or `body_html` (as in NewDiscussion) replaces the whole text; a plain-text `body` would lose links, mentions or formatting, so for a discussion whose text has them (`viewer.can_edit_text` is false) it is 409 formatted_text: send `body_html`. Who may see it does not change here.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Delete a discussion, with its replies
delete.description: One's own where the membership level may delete discussions, or any for administrators and the admins of the group it is in (the module's delete check; 403 otherwise). Its replies, its activity in the feeds and its files go with it, as on the site.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: Events the viewer may find, upcoming ones first
get.description: `when=upcoming` (the default) lists the events that have not ended, ongoing ones and repeating ones that still repeat included, by their start, soonest first; `past` the ones that ended, the latest start first. `from` and `to` keep the events that overlap that time (a month for a calendar), by their start; with them `when` is only applied when sent. Public events, ones for site members when signed in, and closed ones (name, dates and picture only, `content_visible` false), as the site's browse lists; secret events are never listed here. `author` keeps the events a profile made (their public ones, as on their profile page); `context` the events in a group or space (v2 also takes it as `context_id`, the name GET /discussions uses), to those who may see its content: 422 `not_found` for an id that is no context or one the viewer may not know of (a secret one from outside, as for an id with no profile), `invalid_value` for a context of a kind that keeps no events (an event), 403 when the viewer may know of it but not see what is in it (a closed one from outside).

parameters.name: when
parameters.description: Upcoming (the default without `from` and `to`) or past

parameters.name: author
parameters.description: Only events this profile made

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Only events in this group or space

parameters.name: context_id
parameters.description: The same as `context` (v2 only); not with it

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only events that end after this time (v2 only)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only events that start before this time (v2 only); after `from`

get.summary: An event, with the viewer's answer and membership
get.description: With `body_html`. The id is the event's profile id. 404 for a secret event the viewer is neither in nor invited to, for one that is not active (to all but its moderators) and for a profile that is no event; 403 for one the viewer may not see at all. A closed event seen from outside has its name, dates, place and picture (`content_visible` false), as its page on the site.

get.summary: Who is going to an event, in the order they answered
get.description: The event's members, the first to join first, each `going` (with `role`, v2 only). `status=maybe` is an empty page: the site keeps no maybe. To those who may see the event's content (403 for a closed event seen from outside, as its members on the site).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only those with this answer

put.summary: Say the acting profile is going to an event
put.description: Answers the Event. `going` joins the event as POST /groups/{id}/membership joins a group: at once for an open event or one that invited the viewer (`viewer.rsvp` going), as a request to its organisers for one that approves its members (`viewer.status` pending, `rsvp` still null). Saying it again is not an error. `maybe` is 422 `unsupported`: the site keeps no such answer. 403 when the event refuses, 409 `questionnaire_required` or `paid_join` when joining needs the site. An event that has ended is not refused (the site lets one join it).

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Withdraw the acting profile's answer: leave the event, withdraw a request or decline an invitation
delete.description: As DELETE /groups/{id}/membership. Having no answer is not an error.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

post.summary: Post to the viewer's timeline or to a context (group, event, ...)

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

patch.summary: Edit a feed post: its text or who can see it
patch.description: The id is an Activity id. The site's edit check applies: one's own posts where the site lets authors edit, any for moderators; reposts and content of other modules are not editable (403). `body_html` replaces the whole text (the site filters it, and does not clear a post's text: an empty one keeps the old). The post's media and location stay as they are. A post in a context keeps the context's audience (422 on `audience`).

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: The home feed mixed with hot posts
The viewer's own posts and what they follow

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: Posts with the most activity lately
Everything public on the site, newest first
Files the viewer may see, newest first or in another order
get.description: As the site's browse pages list them: active files (never folders), with the module's privacy, so a page can have fewer items than `limit` and still a `next_cursor`. Without `author` or `context` it has the files outside groups and other contexts only, as the site's browse pages: those in a context are in its list (`context`), their author's (`author`) and search (GET /search/files), wherever the viewer may see them. `sort`: `recent` (the default, newest first), `updated`, `popular` (most viewed), `top` (most liked) or `featured` (featured ones only). `author` keeps one profile's files, those in groups and other contexts the viewer may see too (v2 differs from the site's author page, which lists the ones outside contexts), `context` (or `context_id`, as Discussions name it) those in a group or other context: 422 for one that is no context or that the viewer may not know of, 403 for one whose content the viewer may not see. The files in a folder are listed with the others: folders stay on the site.

parameters.name: author
parameters.description: A profile id

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Only files in this group (or other context): its profile id

parameters.name: context_id
parameters.description: The same as `context` (v2 only)

post.summary: Add files: one for each upload
post.description: As the site's upload form adds them: each of `media_ids` (up to 20 of the viewer's uploads of purpose `file`, POST /uploads, that nothing took yet; 422 otherwise) becomes a file, in this order, and the answer lists them so. `title` is every file's title, each upload's file name without its extension when absent. `text_html` is every file's description: user HTML the site filters as its edit form does (or plain text, each line a paragraph). `context_id` puts them in a group (or another context) whose members may add files there (403 otherwise); their audience is then the context's, so `audience` may not be sent with it. `comments_enabled` false is 422: the site can't turn comments off. The site's form checks apply (422 with its message). The site adds them one by one while the membership level's limit of files allows (403 when it allows none): when it stops part way the answer is still 201, with the files made, and the uploads not taken are the ones no file's `media.id` in it is; they stay the viewer's, to send again later or delete (DELETE /uploads/{id}). A video among them is put in the queue of the module's converter, as its page does when it is first shown, so it plays once converted. The category is the upload form's first. A file's name is seen by whoever sees it, as on the site.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: A file the viewer may see, with its description and download
get.description: Counts a view, as opening it on the site does (once a day per viewer). `media.download_url` is the file itself (a private one's link carries a token valid for a few minutes: ask again for a fresh one before a download that waited). 404 when there is none (or it is a folder, or hidden or waiting for approval and the viewer is not its author or a moderator, or in a secret group or other context the viewer may not know of), 403 when the viewer may not see it (one in a closed context from outside). Its comments are GET /content/{content_id}/comments.

patch.summary: Change a file's title, description or audience
patch.description: One's own, or any for moderators (the module's edit check; 403 otherwise). The file itself does not change here: add a new one instead. `audience` is not for one in a context (422).

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

delete.summary: Delete a file
delete.description: One's own where the membership level may delete files, or any for administrators (the module's delete check; 403 otherwise). The stored file, its copies, comments and activity in the feeds go with it, as on the site.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid

get.summary: Groups the viewer may find, newest first
get.description: As the site's browse page lists them (active groups whose privacy lets the viewer find them): public ones, groups for site members when signed in, and closed ones, which show their name and picture only (`content_visible` false) until one joins. Secret groups are never listed here; their members find them in GET /me/groups.

get.summary: A group, with the viewer's membership
get.description: The id is the group's profile id. 404 for a secret group the viewer is neither in nor invited to (as for one that does not exist); 403 for a group the viewer may not see at all (one for site members, to a guest). A closed group seen from outside has its name and picture only (`content_visible` false): its feed and members answer 403 until one joins. `viewer` says what POST and DELETE /groups/{id}/membership and POST /feed-posts with this `context_id` would do.

get.summary: A group's members, most recently joined first

counter.description: The number the site shows beside it (unread messages, friend requests, one's posts), read for the viewer; null for none

target.description: Where it opens in the apps; null for nowhere (an app that can't open `link` leaves it out)

tabs.description: Its submenu's items for the apps (a module's Latest, Popular ...), one level: theirs have no `tabs`

contexts.description: In a `followings` group: the contexts of this module the viewer belongs to (or follows), the newest first, at most 10; [] elsewhere

more_contexts.description: There are more of them than `contexts` has

all_target.description: In a Member Memberships group: where all of them open (All your groups: the module's section at the ones one joined, view `joined`; All your friends: `persons` at `friends`, or `connections` at `friends` on a site without Persons' section); null elsewhere and for a module without a section in the apps. `target` is where the module's contexts are browsed

config.description: Studio's "Config API" of the item ({"button":true} for Log in and Sign up); {} for none

hidden_on.description: The screens it is hidden on ("Hidden on"); on the platform asked for it is never hidden

NavigationTarget.description: Where an item opens in the apps. `section`: a part of the app, `section` names it (`home`, `explore`, `connections`, or the tag of a module's paths: `notifications`, `conversations`, `posts`, `discussions`, `groups`, `spaces`, `events`, `tasks`, `videos`, `photos`, `persons` ...) and `view` a part of it (a module's `popular`, `new`, `mine`, `joined`, `followed`, `favorites`; People's (`persons`) `recent`, `active`, `online` and `friends`, the viewer's; Connections' `friends`, `requests`, `following`, `followers`). `profile` and `context`: the profile with that `id` (of `module`). `page`: the site page at `path`, for GET /layout/resolve. Any kind has `path` when the page it is on the site resolves for the viewer, so a client without a screen of its own for it draws that page. Clients skip kinds and sections they don't know, after trying `path`.

text.description: What the viewer writes, plain text; at most the agent's `max_input_chars`

text_html.description: User HTML the site filters, or plain text (each line a paragraph)

media_ids.description: Uploads of purpose `album` (POST /uploads), its items in this order. v2 differs: photos only

comments_enabled.description: false is 422: the site can't turn comments off

body.description: Plain text, kept as written (a literal `<` stays text); each line is a paragraph

body_html.description: HTML as the site's comment editor writes it (paragraphs, line breaks, links, mentions as `<a class="bx-mention-link" data-profile-id>`, hashtags); the site filters it as its comment form does

parent_id.description: Reply to this comment of the item (a Comment id)

media_ids.description: Uploads of purpose `conversation`, in display order

NewDiscussion.description: A title and one of `body` and `body_html`.

body.description: Plain text; each line a paragraph. Or `body_html`

body_html.description: HTML as the site's editor writes it; the site's form filters it. Or `body`

category_id.description: GET /discussions/categories; the first one by default

context_id.description: A group to start it in; not with `audience`

NewFeedPost.description: A post needs `body_html`, `media_ids`, `links` or more of them.

context_id.description: Post in this group, event or other context instead of the viewer's timeline

media_ids.description: The viewer's uploads (Media ids from POST /uploads) to show in the post, in this order. An id that is not an upload of the viewer's, or one a post already took, is 422.

text_html.description: Every file's description: user HTML the site filters, or plain text (each line a paragraph)

comments_enabled.description: false is 422: the site can't turn comments off

media_ids.description: Uploads of purpose `message`, in display order

NewPhotos.description: Photos to add, one for each upload.

media_ids.description: Uploads of purpose `photo` (POST /uploads), in order. Each becomes a photo

text_html.description: Every photo's text: user HTML the site filters, or plain text (each line a paragraph)

comments_enabled.description: false is 422: the site can't turn comments off

NewPoll.description: A new poll, with who sees it (a poll is an entry of its own, not one put on another item).

question.description: Plain text, each line a paragraph

options.description: 2 to 10 answers, in display order, none given twice

hidden_results.description: Show counts only to people who voted

context_id.description: v2 only. A group (or other context) to put it in; not with `audience`

NewPost.description: A new post. It is published at once, and photos, videos, polls and anonymous posts are added on the site.

summary.description: Plain text. Taken from the text when absent

body_html.description: User HTML the site filters; plain text becomes paragraphs

context_id.description: A group (or other context) to post into; the viewer must be allowed to post there

category_id.description: One of GET /posts/categories; required where the site's form requires a category

media_ids.description: Not taken here: attach photos and videos on the site

comments_enabled.description: False only where the site's form offers it to the viewer

state_id.description: Backlog by default as on the site; a done one adds it completed

hours.description: Whole hours, not 0; below 0 takes hours off

date.description: The day it was spent on; today by default

Platform.description: The kind of client the page or menu is for: `web` ("Hidden on" its three screens), `mobile-app` or `desktop-app` (a desktop app, which follows the desktop screen)

Poll.description: A poll. A poll is an entry of the Polls module, not something put on another item; `content_id` is the Item that shows it in the feeds (its comments and reactions are the poll's), null when the Timeline shows none. One answer per voter, never changed: `voters` is the sum of the votes.

content_id.description: The Item that shows it (GET /content/{id}); null when the Timeline shows none

text_html.description: v2 only: the question as the site keeps it (user HTML the site filtered: sanitize it again before showing it). Only on single answers (GET /polls/{id}, a vote, a new poll); null in lists and feed items

voters.description: How many people voted; always shown

hidden_results.description: The counts are shown only to people who voted

results_visible.description: Whether the options' `votes` are filled for this viewer

image.description: v2 only: the picture its author chose for it, as the module's copies (the original for its owner only); null for none

context_id.description: v2 only: the group or other context it is in

url.description: v2 only: its page on the site

viewer.description: null for guests (they see the results the poll shows everyone, and vote on the site)

title.description: Plain text

votes.description: null while the results are hidden from the viewer (`results_visible` false)

PollViewer.description: The viewer's part in a poll; null for guests.

voted.description: The option they chose; null before they voted

can_vote.description: They have not voted, the poll is published and approved, and their membership level may vote in polls. A vote is never changed or taken back

can_delete.description: v2 only: the module's delete check (DELETE /polls/{id})

Post.description: A post of the Posts module, with its `content_id`, `module` and `url`. Its comments and reactions are those of the Item `content_id` (GET and POST /content/{content_id}/comments, PUT /content/{content_id}/reaction); the feeds' Item of a post names it (`Item.entry_id`).

content_id.description: v2 only. The Item that shows it in the feeds: its comments and reactions are the post's. Null when the Timeline shows none

summary.description: Plain text: the summary its author wrote (the site's abstract), else the start of the text

body_html.description: The text as the site keeps it (user HTML the site filtered: sanitize it again before showing it). Only on single answers (GET, POST and PATCH of one); null in lists

author.description: Null for an anonymous post (except to its author: only they see who wrote it), or an author who is gone

context_id.description: The group or other context it is in

state.description: `scheduled` while it waits for its publishing time, `processing` while a video of it is converted (seen by its author and moderators only)

cover.description: The cover, as the module's copies (`variants`); its original (`url`) only for its owner

media.description: The photos and videos attached to it, as the module's copies. Only on single answers: empty in lists (v2 differs)

links.description: Previews of the http and https links attached to it. Only on single answers: empty in lists (v2 differs)

poll.description: Always null. Polls on posts are made and answered on the site

reading_minutes.description: Its words at 200 a minute, at least 1

revision.description: The site keeps no revisions: always 1 (v2 differs)

url.description: v2 only. Its page on the site

viewer.description: What the viewer did with it and may do (its reaction, favourite and comment rights on single answers only); null for guests

publish_at.description: When a scheduled post is published; null otherwise

PostCategory.description: A post category. The site keeps no slugs: `slug` is the category's value on the site.

count.description: How many posts it has (v2 only, with `counts=true`)

PostChanges.description: Fields to change, omitted ones stay. The cover, photos, videos and publishing change on the site, and no revision is kept.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem document. `code` is stable and meant for programs.

title.description: Short summary of the status, in English

detail.description: Explanation of this occurrence, in English. Not for end users.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code; clients localize from it

Profile.description: A profile, with `module` and `url`. Embedded in other resources (authors, actors, members, search hits) it has no description or cover: `about` is empty and `cover` null; GET /profiles/{id} has them.

module.description: The UNA module the profile belongs to (v2 only)

handle.description: The last part of the profile page's address on the site, for GET /profiles/by-handle/{handle}; null when the site has none

about.description: Plain text, at most 1000 characters: a longer description is cut, ending in …. Empty in an embedded profile

about_truncated.description: The description is longer than `about` carries; PATCH /profiles/{id} does not change such an about (409 `too_long`): it is edited on the site. Not in an embedded profile (v2 only)

avatar.description: The square picture (100x100); null when there is none or the viewer may not see it. An absolute URL; resolve it against the API's origin (`new URL(avatar, origin)`)

avatar_large.description: The same picture at 200x200, for large places; null exactly when `avatar` is. Not in an embedded profile (v2 only)

cover.description: The wide banner; null in an embedded profile

url.description: The profile page on the site (v2 only)

created_at.description: When the profile joined. In an embedded profile only for a viewer who may open the profile's page; otherwise, and for a profile with no date (the site's own), `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`: unknown

badges.description: The badges the site shows next to the name, to any viewer, in the order to show them; left out when the profile has none

ProfileAction.description: An item of the More menu of a profile's or a context's page that the apps do themselves (GET /profiles/{id}/actions).

name.description: The site's name of the menu item

title.description: What the site's item says

icon.description: A Lucide icon name: Studio's icon of the item as the site's Lucide set draws it, else the action's own

action.description: `report`: POST /profiles/{id}/report with one of `choices`; `edit`: the profile's editor (PATCH /profiles/{id})

done.description: `report`: the viewer has reported it (a second report is 409); false otherwise

choices.description: `report`: the site's reasons, in its order; null otherwise

ProfileBadge.description: A badge given to a profile (Studio > Badges)

name.description: The badge's text in the viewer's language, sent for an `icon_only` badge too, where it labels the icon for screen readers; may be empty

icon.description: A Lucide icon name; null when the badge has none, or one that is not a Lucide or Font Awesome name (an uploaded image, which is `image`; an emoji)

color.description: The badge's colour, CSS hex; null when the site's value is not a colour

image.description: The picture uploaded as the badge's icon: an absolute URL of a 180x180 square copy; resolve it against the API's origin. Clients draw it instead of `icon`. Left out when the badge has none, or its picture is an SVG, which has no such copy

icon_only.description: The site shows the badge as its icon or `image` alone, without `name` (Studio's "Icon only"); clients do too and give `name` to screen readers and tooltips. Left out when false

ProfileChanges.description: What to change in a profile; at least one field.

display_name.description: The name the profile goes by; the site's own checks of the name apply

about.description: Plain text that replaces the whole about; each line becomes a paragraph, an empty one clears it

avatar_id.description: An upload of purpose `profile` for the picture; null takes the picture off

cover_id.description: An upload of purpose `profile` for the cover; null takes the cover off

ProfileReport.description: A report of a profile or a context.

text.description: A note for the moderators, plain text

kind.description: A reaction name, or an emoji where the site lets people pick any

title.description: In the viewer's language; the name a screen reader says, whichever way it is drawn

emoji.description: Empty when the reaction has none

icon.description: A Lucide icon name: the reaction's Lucide or Font Awesome icon, and for a Font Awesome face Lucide has no icon for, the Lucide face NEO's web set draws (`laugh-squint` is `laugh`, `surprise` is `smile`, `sad-tear` is `frown`); null for none

color.description: The reaction's colour on the site as CSS hex; null for none

display.description: How the site draws its reactions: as their icons (a kind without one as its emoji) or as emoji, by most of the reactions' Icon / Emoji / Image choice in Studio (an image counts as an icon)

per_user.description: How many different reactions one person may give

any_emoji.description: Any single emoji may be given as a reaction

Realtime.description: Where to listen for live events: a Pusher-protocol sockets server and the public channels for what a client shows

enabled.description: The site has a sockets server; without one, poll GET /sync alone

url.description: The WebSocket to open (ws or wss), with the app key and protocol 7 in it

key.description: The app key the server knows the site by (public: it is in every site page that listens)

channels.description: Public channels by what they carry: `activities` (the feed), `connections` (the viewer's friendships and follows). More may come: skip a name you do not know

request_sent.description: The viewer asked to be friends and waits

request_received.description: The profile asked to be friends; POST /profiles/{id}/friend accepts

blocking.description: Always false: UNA has no blocking of profiles

can_follow.description: POST /profiles/{id}/follow would make a new follow

can_befriend.description: POST /profiles/{id}/friend would send a request or accept one

ResolvedBlock.description: A block of a page, without its data: the client reads `endpoint`.

kind.description: What it shows and so how it is drawn: `timeline.public`, `timeline.home`, `timeline.hot`, `timeline.for_you`, `timeline.compose` (the composer, no endpoint), `graph.friends`, `graph.friend_suggestions`, `graph.follow_suggestions`, `posts.list` and the other modules' `<tag>.list`, `groups.joined` and the like; also `profile.info` (a profile's Info, GET /profiles/{id}/info), `groups.members`, `spaces.members` and `events.members` (a context's Members), `posts.categories` and `discussions.categories` (a module's categories with their counts), `text.html` (text written in Studio, a language string or HTML: GET /layout/blocks/{id}/text). Clients skip kinds they don't know

module.description: The module that feeds it (v2 only)

title.description: Its title in the viewer's language; empty for none

title_key.description: Always null in v2: `title` is translated

endpoint.description: The GET route it reads, under the API's base, with its query; for a paged one add `cursor` for more. Null for one with no data (the composer)

uri.description: The page's path on the site: `/` for the home page, `/page/<uri>` for another

params.description: The values of the path's query

cells.description: The layout's cells in reading order, empty ones included

Screen.description: A screen a block, or a part of its frame, can be hidden on: the web's three widths (phone, tablet, desktop; the desktop app takes them from the width of its content) and the mobile app. UNA's names

Space.description: A space: a context like a group (Group's fields, kind `group`, module `bx_spaces`), which may be in another space and have subspaces.

module.description: The UNA module the profile belongs to (v2 only)

handle.description: The last part of the profile page's address on the site, for GET /profiles/by-handle/{handle}; null when the site has none

about.description: Plain text, at most 1000 characters: a longer description is cut, ending in …. Empty in an embedded profile

about_truncated.description: The description is longer than `about` carries; PATCH /profiles/{id} does not change such an about (409 `too_long`): it is edited on the site. Not in an embedded profile (v2 only)

avatar.description: The square picture (100x100); null when there is none or the viewer may not see it. An absolute URL; resolve it against the API's origin (`new URL(avatar, origin)`)

avatar_large.description: The same picture at 200x200, for large places; null exactly when `avatar` is. Not in an embedded profile (v2 only)

cover.description: The wide banner; null in an embedded profile

url.description: The profile page on the site (v2 only)

created_at.description: When the profile joined. In an embedded profile only for a viewer who may open the profile's page; otherwise, and for a profile with no date (the site's own), `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`: unknown

badges.description: The badges the site shows next to the name, to any viewer, in the order to show them; left out when the profile has none

join_policy.description: open: joining makes a member at once; approval: it asks the admins of the group (or other context)

content_visible.description: Whether the viewer may see its about, cover, feed and members; false for a closed one seen from outside

content_kinds.description: The tags of the modules whose content may be added in a context of this module (v2 only): `discussions` when GET /discussions?context_id= lists its discussions and POST /discussions takes it as `context_id`. The same for every context of the module, and whether the viewer may add is that endpoint's check. Posts (the feed) are not listed: `viewer.can_post` says those

viewer.description: The acting profile's membership; null for guests

parent_id.description: The space this one is in (GET /spaces/{id}); null for a top level space, and for one whose parent the viewer may not know of (a secret one) or that is not active

child_count.description: How many subspaces GET /spaces/{id}/spaces lists to the viewer (secret ones are not counted; 0 for a closed space seen from outside, whose subspaces that path refuses)

Suggestion.description: A profile the site suggests to the acting profile (v2 only), with the site's points for the match.

cursor.description: Send it with the next sync

changes.description: What changed since the cursor. Here the new notifications (`type` `notification`, `data` a Notification), newest first, when the site has Notifications; skip a `type` you do not know

lists.description: New entries by list name, for the heads sent: always empty here, since GET /sync sends none

more.description: More changes are waiting: sync again at once with this cursor

reset.description: The cursor was another profile's: reload lists

Task.description: A task. Its comments and reactions are those of the Item `content_id`.

summary.description: The start of its text, as plain text

body_html.description: Its text as the site keeps it (user HTML the site filtered: sanitize it again before showing it). Only on single answers; null in lists

context_id.description: The group (or other context) it is in; null for one added outside any on the site

list_id.description: Its list in the context; null: the context's Inbox (or no context)

list_title.description: Its list's title, the Inbox's as the site names it; null for one in no context

assignees.description: Who it is assigned to, the first assigned first

due_at.description: When it is due; null for no due date

state.description: Its state on the context's board (Backlog, To do ...). Completing it does not change it, as on the site

type.description: Bug, Feature ... (the context's own where it has them)

labels.description: Its labels (the site's stickers; the context's own, with their colours, where it has them)

time_spent.description: All the time logged on it, in seconds (whole minutes)

timer.description: The viewer's timer on it; null for none (and for guests)

content_id.description: The Item that shows it in the feeds, whose comments and reactions are its; null when the Timeline shows none

viewer.description: What the viewer may do; null for guests

TaskBudget.description: A context's budget of time (the module's bx_tasks_budget, kept in minutes): what its entries add, what is logged on its tasks.

total_seconds.description: What its entries add (their hours); below 0 when they take off more than they add

spent_seconds.description: The time logged on the context's tasks since it has a budget

remaining_seconds.description: total less spent: below 0 when more is spent

remaining_percent.description: remaining of total, in percent (two decimals; below 0 when more is spent); null while the total is not above 0

TaskBudgetEntry.description: Hours added to (or taken off) a context's budget.

hours.description: Whole hours; below 0 takes hours off

TaskBudgetEntryChanges.description: What to change; what is left out stays.

TaskChanges.description: Fields to change; omitted ones stay, and so do nulls but for `due_at`, `list_id` (the Inbox), `priority_id`, `type_id` and `estimate_id`, where null is none.

title.description: As the site's form takes it (its own checks apply too: 422 with its message)

body.description: Replaces the whole text: plain text, each line a paragraph

label_ids.description: Replacing those it has; [] for none

state_id.description: GET /tasks/choices `states`; a done one completes the task, another one reopens it

assignee_ids.description: Members of the context, replacing those it has; [] for nobody

TaskChoice.description: A type, priority, estimate, state or label the site offers a task (its form's pre-values, in the viewer's language; a context's own types and labels where it has them).

done.description: States only: whether the site counts a task in it as done (Cancelled, Duplicate, Done)

points.description: Estimates only: its points (the site's task list shows a point as an hour)

color.description: Labels only: a CSS colour (#hex, rgb() or rgba()) the context gave it; null for none

module_title.description: Its kind as the site names it (Groups, Spaces ...)

lists.description: The Inbox first, then its lists in the order they were made

can_view_budget.description: May see and change its budget (GET /task-contexts/{id}/budget): its administrators and the site's

id.description: The value (a choice, a profile); null for none

TaskFacets.description: How many tasks a list has, open and completed, by each property.

labels.description: A task under each of its labels; null: those with none

assignees.description: A task under each of its assignees

kind.description: The site's, the context's for everyone, or the viewer's own

TaskIdList.description: Ids of GET /tasks/choices, comma-separated: a task with any of them

TaskList.description: A context's task list; `id` null is its Inbox, the tasks in no list.

id.description: The list; null for the context's Inbox

title.description: As the site's form takes it (its own checks apply too: 422 with its message)

can_edit.description: May rename it (false for the Inbox)

can_delete.description: May delete it with its tasks (the context's administrators; false for the Inbox)

items.description: The Inbox first, then the lists in the order they were made

total_seconds.description: All the time logged on the task

all.description: Whether `items` are everyone's (the site's report_view check); else the viewer's own

TaskTimer.description: The viewer's timer on a task.

seconds.description: What it has counted, until the answer was made

started_at.description: When it was (re)started; null while paused

items.description: Each with its `timer`, the running one first

can_edit.description: May change its title and text (its author, moderators)

can_track_time.description: May run a timer on it and log time (who may complete it, where the site lets them log time)

can_complete.description: May complete or reopen it, and change its list, priority, state, due date and assignees (its author, moderators, the context's administrators and its assignees; false for one in no context)

can_delete.description: Read on single answers only (false in lists)

can_comment.description: Read on single answers only (false in lists)

can_react.description: Read on single answers only (false in lists)

reaction.description: The viewer's reaction; read on single answers only (null in lists)

date.description: The day it was spent on

file.description: A photo or a video, with its file name (the extension says which)

purpose.description: What takes it: `post` (POST /feed-posts), and where the Conversations module is on, `message` (POST /conversations/{id}/messages) and `conversation` (POST /conversations), which take photos only, and `profile` (PATCH /profiles/{id}: a picture or cover of the acting profile), photos only too; where the Videos module is on, `video` (POST /videos), videos only, which its own transcoders convert (`state` processing until GET /uploads/{id} says ready); where the Photos module is on, `photo` (POST /photos), photos only; where the Albums module is on, `album` (POST /albums and POST /albums/{id}/items), photos only; where the Files module is on, `file` (POST /files), a file of any type its storage takes (photos and videos must be what their names say); where the Posts module is on, `post_cover` (POST /posts `cover_media_id`), photos only. Another is 422.

width.description: The original's size fitted into the copy's box (the site keeps no sizes of its copies); 0 when not known

session.name: memberSession
session.description: The site's own session cookie, for pages of the site itself. Requests that change something must come from the site's origin.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2 authorization code flow with PKCE (S256). Native apps use a public client and a loopback redirect (RFC 8252); the port may vary.

scopes.api: Act as the signed-in profile through API v2

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before sending the request again

idempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotencyKey.description: Any unique string (a UUID) for this write; send the same one again to retry it safely: the first answer comes back for a day
